title: trailboss --json team start
description: One object: the plan `team start <team> --task …` shows (no --yes), or with --yes the plan approved and the lead started, alone, in a new host terminal in the folder; it starts the members within the plan. The command runs directly, never through a shell. Refused at --yes when a role's definition has a problem or no host is running. Frontends should show an action they don't know as is.

action.description: would start (no --yes) or started; more may be added.

n.description: The team's number, for `team status` and `team stop`; in the plan, the number it would get.

path.description: The team's file; null for a built-in one.

trust.description: A repository team's trust: always trusted here (an untrusted one is refused). Null for yours and built-in ones.

folder.description: The folder the team works in, where the lead starts.

lead.description: Whether it's the lead's role: its one member is the lead `team start --yes` starts.

agent.description: The agent definition its members start from (`agents ls`).

works.description: How its members work: task (its own git worktree and branch, started with `task add --role`), review (one of the team's tasks, with `task review --role`) or shared-readonly (in the team's folder, to read and plan, with `start --role`); more may be added.

count.description: The most members of it that may start, over the team's whole run.

description.description: What its members do, from the team file.

kind.description: The agent kind the definition starts: claude, codex, …; null when it has a problem.

source.description: Where the definition comes from: repo, user or built-in; null when it has a problem.

path.description: The definition's file; null for a built-in one.

trust.description: A repository definition's trust (always trusted when resolved); null for yours and built-in ones.

command.description: What a member runs, its brief shown as `<brief>`; null when it has a problem.

problem.description: Why the definition can't start as things are (unknown, broken, a repository's not trusted); null when it can.

roles.description: The roster the plan approves: each role, its definition, how members work and how many may start.

dollars.description: The most the team may spend: --dollars, else the team's, else 20. At it no more members start.

hours.description: The most hours it may run: --hours, else the team's, else 4.

estimate_usd.description: What it might cost with every member started: each at the average cost of recent sessions of its agent kind in the index; null with no sessions to go by.

estimate_basis.description: What the estimate is based on, per agent kind.

host.description: herdr, tmux, …; null when no host is running (the plan then says so).

terminal.description: The lead's terminal's address, once started.

command.description: What the lead runs, its first prompt (its definition's rules, then the team's guide and the task) shown as `<brief>`; null when its definition has a problem.

parent.description: AGENT:ID of the session `team start` ran in.

detail.description: The plan in a line: the lead, how many more members, the limits and the estimate; anything that stops it from starting.
